description:
ir_interp/value.rs interp_runtime_type_predicate_schema_ids builds both halves of RuntimeValueReader's schema maps on EVERY call: the tuple half registers a schema per arity the predicate names, and the named half loops every module.struct_schemas entry, cloning the name and the field list into SchemaRegistry::register, which is a linear scan with a deep assert_eq per entry. Its callers are whole_value_matches_predicate (ir_interp/backend.rs ~917) and therefore every RuntimeTypeTest step and every AssertTuple that misses the transport fast path -- once per execution, not once per module.

Measured on a mailbox-delivered tuple destructured in a loop, release build, fz2 interp, best of five. 40k iterations: 0 named structs 0.28s, 48 live named structs 1.87s. 2M iterations: 0 named structs 13.59s, 48 live named structs 88.22s -- about 37us of pure table rebuilding per call, scaling with the module rather than with the question.

fz-wof took the cheap half: it skips the named loop entirely for a predicate that reads no named schema, via RuntimeTypePredicate::reads_named_schemas (the named-structs axis, or either struct axis whose arity set is cofinite, at any depth). That took the 48-struct probe to 0.42s / 14.07s. What is left is the shape: the reader's schema maps are a property of the MODULE plus the arities in play, so they should be built once and handed to the matcher, not rebuilt per call. The per-call registration is also why schema ids depend on execution order rather than on the module.

Same debt, other door: native_codegen/runtime_test.rs ~469 emit_named_struct_axis collects named ids out of a HashMap, so the order of the emitted compares follows hash order. Folding both onto one module-scoped, ordered table settles them together.
title: The interpreter rebuilds its schema-id reader per matcher call instead of once per module
